segments.t: Armed with a kitchen knife just in case, Senya and Fedya creep out to the courtyard to scare the photographer sitting in a car outside the restaurant. The plan goes horribly wrong when Fedya panics during the confrontation and accidentally knocks the man out cold.
Если тебе хлеба вдруг внезапно нужно будет нарезать?
Давай, ты иди, я на шутку поставлю.
Слушай, зачем же я пошёл с тобой?
Right, let's take their exchange slowly and unpack the Russian.

'We will just scare him a little, right?' Wondering if they will just scare him a little right shows Kostya caught off guard. In Russian, he does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.
'What do you need this knife for?' By asking what Kostya needs this knife, Nastya presses Kostya for a straight answer.
'Just in case.' Over the truth and the shift, Kostya answers Nastya without a second thought.
Если тебе хлеба вдруг внезапно нужно будет нарезать?

'In case you suddenly need to slice some bread?' Over the restaurant and the car, Nastya presses Kostya for a straight answer. There is no "you" needed in the Russian here: one short word states the rule for everyone in the room.
'We agreed we are only going to scare him.' Adding that they agreed they are only going to scare him fills in the missing piece for Nastya.
Давай, ты иди, я на шутку поставлю.

'Go on, you go ahead and I will keep watch.' Going on Kostya goes ahead and she will keep watch moves the conversation forward without extra drama. Starting with "davay" is the everyday Russian way to say "come on, let us do this".
'It is nothing, come on, get going.' Since it is nothing come on get going, Kostya does not waste words on excuses. Starting with "davay" is the everyday Russian way to say "come on, let us do this".
'Guys, what on earth is going on?' When Nastya asks if what on earth is going, Kostya has to answer fast.
'Keep quiet, keep quiet, hush!' Telling Nastya to keep quiet keep quiet hush shows Kostya is done holding back. Using the informal "you" shows how direct and unfiltered their kitchen relationship is.
'What have you done?' Asking whether what have Kostya done puts Kostya right on the defensive. Speaking with the close, informal "you" strips away any polite distance between them.
'I just wanted to scare him a little.' Explaining that he just wanted to scare him a little lays the cards on the table for Nastya.

'Why did you even touch him at all?' Asking why Kostya even touch him at all is how Nastya puts Kostya on the spot. Speaking with the close, informal "you" strips away any polite distance between them.
Слушай, зачем же я пошёл с тобой?

'Listen, why on earth did I go with you?' When Kostya asks if why on earth did he goes with Nastya, Nastya has to answer fast. Using the informal "you" shows how direct and unfiltered their kitchen relationship is. Now let's listen to the entire scene again without interruption.
Если тебе хлеба вдруг внезапно нужно будет нарезать?
Давай, ты иди, я на шутку поставлю.
Слушай, зачем же я пошёл с тобой?
That wraps up this scene as senya and Fedya sneak out to intimidate the man sitting in a parked car outside Claude Monet, but Fedya accidentally knocks him unconscious. See you next time!
